extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students (or other learners) using the Proof Designer applet to write proofs in elementary set theory / discrete mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Interactive guidance for writing formal proofs in elementary set theory using the Proof Designer Java applet: enter hypotheses and conclusion, work through gaps (givens and goals), add steps via the menus, use subproofs and variants, and export the resulting proof. The page also gives a brief summary of proof techniques and specific UI actions (menus/commands) for Proof Designer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input notation for hypotheses and conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: "The hypotheses and conclusion are entered using ordinary set-theoretic and logical notation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter hypotheses and conclusion into the dialog box that appears when you click "Write a Proof." Follow the website's typing rules; note the significant distinction enforced by Proof Designer on intersections of families of sets (the NF notation): Proof Designer restricts contexts where NF can be used (see website / exercise 14 of Section 2.3 for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Start proof: initial gap with givens and goal
rubrics_metrics.description: When you start a proof the window opens with the theorem statement and a place where the proof will go; initially the entire proof is a single gap whose givens are the hypotheses of the theorem and whose goal is the conclusion of the theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this initial gap as your top-level goal; subsequent work fills this gap by adding steps, subproofs, and variants until the goal is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Edit / Strategy / Infer menus to add steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proof Designer window contains three menus, called “Edit,” “Strategy,” and “Infer.” To add a step to the proof, select a given or a goal (or several items) and then give a command from one of these menus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commands require selecting multiple items: select the first item, hold the shift key, and click additional items to add them to the selection. Many proof actions are performed via these menus rather than by free-form typing of steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gaps, givens and goals: structure and interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Each gap is an indented boxed region (with a “?” button) that states what needs to be filled, lists the givens (statements known at that point), and shows the goal (the statement to be proven or the variable to assign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You fill a gap by selecting givens/goals and issuing commands; gaps can also have no goal (e.g., places to assign variables). Use the provided givens and goals as the structured context for each proof step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subproofs as justifications and nesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps can be justified by subproofs — sequences of steps that together justify an assertion. Each subproof is indented, enclosed in a box, and has a button (".:.") in the upper left corner; subproofs may be nested and may contain gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a step is selected, any subproofs justifying it are selected as well. Use subproofs to structure conditional arguments, assumptions-for-contradiction, existential proofs, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variants: create and use equivalent forms of givens/goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commands add variant forms to givens or goals. A variant is another statement equivalent to the original; variants are listed below the original and indented, and can be selected and used like the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use variants when a different but equivalent formulation is more convenient for an inference or strategy; variants move with their parent givens when reordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting items and entire gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: You can select a step in the proof by clicking on it; you can select an entire gap by clicking either on the sentence that introduces the gap or in the margin to the left of the gap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To select several givens/goals at once, select the first then hold shift and click additional items. When selecting a step with subproofs, the subproofs are selected together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorder givens by drag-and-drop
rubrics_metrics.description: You can change the order of the givens in a givens list by pointing to a given, pressing and holding the mouse button to “grab” it, and then dragging it to a new location in the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any variants of the given get moved with it. Reordering can be useful to surface the givens most relevant to the current gap or strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hide or show details of subproofs and gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: If the structure of the proof gets complicated, you can hide some of the details by clicking on a “.:.” or “?” button in the upper left corner of a subproof or gap; clicking again shows the details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hiding to manage visual complexity, focusing on the high-level proof outline while preserving the detailed steps for later inspection or refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export / printing workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Applets are not allowed to print directly. Use one of the Export HTML commands to export the proof for printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Proof Designer website for the specific Export HTML options and instructions for getting a printable copy of your proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexpress negative goals as positive statements (Strategy command)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove a goal that is a negative statement, reexpress it as a positive statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Proof Designer: select the goal, give the Reexpress command in the Strategy menu, and use the Reexpress Negative button in the Reexpress dialog box. This converts a negated goal into an equivalent positive form suitable for the available inference steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Proof Designer's syntactic restrictions (NF / family intersections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof Designer enforces a restriction on the use of NF (intersections of families of sets) that differs from the textbook: NF is allowed only in contexts where F ≠ ∅.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Proof Designer enforces this rule, consult the website for detailed typing rules and examples of allowed/forbidden contexts; this prevents entering expressions that would be ill-formed in the applet.
